final.answer: Yes — FV-104-2 (an easy-e valve, variants ET/EAT/ETR) can be supplied with flanged ends, not just buttweld or screwed. Available end connections include RF or RTJ flanged CL150, CL300 and CL600, CL125 FF and CL250 RF flanged (cast iron), and PN16–40 / PN63–100 flanges, in addition to butt weld, socket weld and screwed ends. Note that flanged valves meeting EN 1092 with EN face-to-face dimensions are available only from Europe.

final.answer: The valve operated by loop FIC-106-2 is FV-106-2, a globe control valve. Per its datasheet (Fisher ET/D100022X012), the valve plug seal (seal ring in the plug) is available in several materials. For the 2-piece valve plug seal (standard for NPS 1-6 valves except those with Cavitrol III cage): carbon-filled PTFE from -73 to 232 °C (-100 to 450 °F); ethylene-propylene from -40 to 232 °C (-40 to 450 °F, good with hot water/steam and most fire-resistant hydraulic oils but not petroleum-based fluids and other hydrocarbons); fluorocarbon from -18 to 204 °C (0 to 400 °F, for high-temperature air, hydrocarbons and certain other chemicals and solvents, not for steam or ammonia, not recommended for water above 82 °C/180 °F); and nitrile from -40 to 71 °C (-40 to 160 °F) for air and hydrocarbons or -40 to 82 °C (-40 to 180 °F) for other compatible fluids, but not with fire-resistant hydraulic oils. For the spring-loaded valve plug seal (standard for the NPS 8 valve and all NPS 1-6 valves with Cavitrol III cages, optional otherwise): PTFE with an N10276 spring from -73 to 232 °C (-100 to 450 °F), or PTFE/graphite with an R30003 spring from -73 to 316 °C (-100 to 600 °F), though limited to 260 °C/500 °F in oxidizing service — this is the extended-temperature version (with PEEK anti-extrusion rings: 316 °C/600 °F non-oxidizing, 260 °C/500 °F oxidizing). Other listed parts, such as stainless steel seal ring parts, PEEK anti-extrusion rings and PTFE V-ring packing (-40 to 232 °C / -40 to 450 °F), are noted as not limiting temperature, with other valve parts setting the limits instead. No part explicitly called a piston ring appears in the datasheet.

final.answer: The instrument measuring E-105-2 is FT-105-2, and its datasheet is a Rosemount 3051 ordering guide covering several models (3051C, 3051T, 3051L, 3051CFA/CFC/CFP) rather than one selected unit, so no single confirmed flange connection is specified. That said, 1/4-18 NPT is among the offered process connections: the 3051C offers 1/4-18 NPT on 2 1/8-inch centers, the 3051L low-pressure flange side offers 1/4-18 NPT on flange, and 3051T model code 2B selects a 1/4-18 NPT process connection. Manifolds are available already fitted: factory-assembled integral manifolds (Rosemount 304, 305 or 306, ordering codes S5/S6 on the 3051C) and direct-mount 3- or 5-valve manifold options (e.g. 3051CFA/CFC option 3) can be ordered with the transmitter. To pin down the exact connection for your unit, the specific model number would need to be identified from the ordering tables.

final.answer: For pump P-1-2, the pump specifications list a maximum operating temperature limit of 37 °C (100 °F), with a note to consult the factory for applications exceeding the indicated maximum pressure and/or temperature. The seal detail separately allows a maximum temperature of liquid pumped of 71 °C (160 °F). So the hottest liquid you can put through it is 37 °C (100 °F) per the pump's operating limit (the seal can tolerate up to 71 °C / 160 °F).

final.answer: Yes — GV-10-1 is a solenoid valve (type 165, 2/2-way, PVC-U) and its coil needs electrical power. The valve is available with supply voltages of 24V DC, 230V AC (50/60 Hz) and 110V AC, with a voltage tolerance of ±10%. So either 24 V DC or 230 V AC will work, but only if the matching coil is fitted: which one is correct is decided by the coil actually installed on the valve, and the manufacturer's instruction is to use the voltage and current type given on the type plate (AC coils also carry a risk-of-injury warning). If you need to change voltage, separate coil sets (spare parts) are offered for each of the three voltages.

final.answer: FV-106-2 is a Fisher easy-e globe control valve, and per its datasheet the flow characteristic depends on the cage chosen. With standard cages you can get quick-opening, linear, or equal percentage. With Whisper Trim, WhisperFlo, or Cavitrol cages the characteristic is linear only. final.answer: FIC-104-2 operates control valve FV-104-2, which is described by a Fisher easy-e valve bulletin (ET/EAT/ETR family). The available trim options for this family are: standard metal trims 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 27, 28, 29, 37/37H, 57 and 316L (with variants 37H for temperatures above 210°C and 4C/29C/57C for PTFE seating); NACE sour-service trims 85, 85C, 86, 87, 87C; Trim Cartridge trims (1TC, 27TC, 29TC, 85TC, 87TC); DST (dirty service) trim; Cavitrol III trim (trim 76, one- and two-stage cages); and Whisper noise-attenuation trims (Whisper Trim I, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim and WhisperFlo cages). The trims for high pressure drop or noise are the Whisper trims/cages, which provide aerodynamic noise attenuation for gaseous service, and the Cavitrol III trim (trim 76), which protects against cavitation at high pressure drops in liquid service.

final.answer: GV-1-2 is a globe valve in the discharge line from pump P-1-1, upstream of ball valve PV-1-1. A globe valve passing fluid when it should be shut is usually caused by seat or disc damage — wear, erosion, or debris (e.g., a particle or weld slug) lodged on the sealing face — or a stem/disc connection failure that prevents the disc from seating. Fix it by closing upstream and downstream isolation (note PV-1-1 downstream) and depressurizing/draining the line, then inspect: lap or re-seat the disc and seat ring or replace the trim, replace the gasket if the leak is at the bonnet or flanges, and verify the disc is properly attached to the stem and the valve is fully turned to the closed position before returning to service.

args.question: What is the maximum temperature of the graphite valve packing option for the 3051CFC compact flow meter?

final.answer: The description identifies carbon-filled PTFE, fluorocarbon, nitrile, and PTFE/graphite seal materials. It gives fluorocarbon a minimum of −18 °C (0 °F) and nitrile a maximum of 71 °C (160 °F). A PTFE/carbon seal ring with PEEK anti-extrusion rings is stated to be usable up to 316 °C (600 °F) in non-oxidizing service or 260 °C (500 °F) in oxidizing service; PTFE/graphite with a spring-loaded seal has the same stated upper limits. Other temperature limits are not provided in the description.

final.answer: Yes — per the datasheet for FV-104-2 (Fisher ET), the valve is available with flanged ends, not only buttweld or screwed. Flanged options include cast iron bodies with CL125 FF or CL250 RF flanges, steel bodies with RF or RTJ flanges in CL150/CL300/CL600, and EN flanges (EN1092-1/B, PN16–PN100) on raised-face steel bodies. Butt weld and socket weld are steel-body options, and screwed ends are only offered in NPS 1, 1-1/2 or 2. Exact availability depends on the valve variant, size and body material (Table 3, page 5).

For the HART 4-20 mA output, you change the alarm direction with a jumper/switch on the transmitter (or by ordering the 'Alarm levels' option: high alarm code C4, low alarm code CN, or custom levels CR/CS); default levels are high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA and low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA (NAMUR: ≥ 22.5 mA / ≤ 3.6 mA). For the 1-5 V low-power output, the direction is selected by an internal jumper (high alarm > 5.4 V, low alarm < 0.94 V). Digital outputs (Fieldbus etc.) have no high/low analog alarm direction — failure is passed as an alert/status. The factory standard configuration is alarm = High.

On signal failure the transmitter can drive its output either high or low — the direction is not fixed, but is selected by you, using a jumper/switch on the transmitter (an internal jumper for the 1-5 V low-power output). [p. 88]

Details (all from page 88):

**HART 4-20 mA output (option code A):**
- If self-diagnostics detect a sensor or microprocessor failure, the analog signal is driven either high or low to alert the user.
- High or low failure mode is user-selectable with a jumper/switch on the transmitter.
- The actual current levels depend on how the alarm levels are configured (see Table 5 on page 88, "Failure mode alarm"):
  - Default setting: high alarm ≥ 21.75 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.75 mA (footnote: high alarm default is ≥ 22.5 mA for some options — codes M6, DA1, T9, RK)
  - NAMUR-compliant setting (option codes C4 or CN): high alarm ≥ 22.5 mA, low alarm ≤ 3.6 mA
  - Custom levels: high alarm 20.2–23.0 mA, low alarm 3.6–3.8 mA (footnote: low alarm must be 0.1 mA less than low saturation, and high alarm must be 0.1 mA greater than high saturation)

**1-5 V low-power output (Output code M):**
- On a gross transmitter failure the signal is driven below 0.94 V (low alarm) or above 5.4 V (high alarm).
- High or low alarm signal is user-selectable by internal jumper.

**Digital outputs (codes F, W, X — e.g. FOUNDATION Fieldbus):** there is no high/low analog alarm direction; a gross failure is passed as an alert and a status along with the process variable. [p. 88]

Also worth knowing: when ordering, the alarm direction can be chosen via the "Alarm levels" option — high alarm (code C4), low alarm (code CN), or custom high/low levels (codes CR/CS). This option is only available with the HART 4-20 mA output (code A) [pp. 15, 26, 42, 52, 63, 74]. The standard factory configuration is Alarm = High [p. 109].
